WITH EFFECT FROM THE ACADEMIC YEAR 2022-23
1.0 Under-Graduate Degree Programme in Engineering & Technology (UGP in E&T)
Jawaharlal Nehru Technological University Hyderabad (JNTUH) offers a 4-year (8
semesters) Bachelor of Technology (B.Tech.) degree programme, under Choice
Based Credit System (CBCS) at its non-autonomous constituent and affiliated
colleges with effect from the academic year 2022-23.
2.0 Eligibility for Admission 2.1 Admission to the undergraduate(UG) programme shall be made either on the basis of
the merit rank obtained by the qualified student in entrance test conducted by the
Telangana State Government (EAMCET) or the University or on the basis of any
other order of merit approved by the University, subject to reservations as prescribed
by the government from time to time. 2.2 The medium of instructions for the entire undergraduate programme in Engineering &

3.0 B.Tech. Programme Structure 3.1 A student after securing admission shall complete the B.Tech. programme in a
minimum period of four academic years (8 semesters), and a maximum period of
eight academic years (16 semesters) starting from the date of commencement of first
year first semester, failing which student shall forfeit seat in B.Tech course. Each
student shall secure 160 credits (with CGPA ≥ 5) required for the completion of the
undergraduate programme and award of the B.Tech. degree. 3.2 UGC/ AICTE specified definitions/ descriptions are adopted appropriately for
various terms and abbreviations used in these academic regulations/ norms, which are
listed below. 3.2.1 Semester Scheme

be permitted to appear for the supplementary series examination. Such students need not register
along with their junior batch.
3 Whether the CBT provision is there for the already completed academic years / semesters in R-22
regulations? Ans Yes. The students who have not secured sufficient internal marks to get eligibility to write
semester-end examination and subsequently not registered the same course with their juniors or
registered but could not secure the minimum marks to get the eligibility for appearing semester end
examinations, shall be allowed to appear for the CBT exam.
4 What if the student does not get the required minimum marks in CBT for becoming eligible to
appear for SEE? Ans Such students shall have the following two options: 1) Register for this course along with the next

doc: JNTUH R22 FAQs - Computer Based Test (CBT)
text:
n CBT for becoming eligible to
appear for SEE? Ans Such students shall have the following two options: 1) Register for this course along with the next
batch students of the same branch or 2) writing the CBT once again when the notification is issued.
5 How the CBT exam of R-22 and R-25 regulations are different? Ans In R-25 regulations, the option of CBT is given for every student who wish to improve his/her
internal marks and the average of best two out of three (two mid-term exams plus one CBT) shall
be the final CIE marks. Other assessment components will remain the same.
Where as in R-22 regulations, CBT provision is there only for the students, who could not score
the minimum required marks and CBT exam shall be conducted for the marks that are equal to

maximum marks allocated for CIE. Other assessment components shall not be taken into
consideration.
6 Whether the CBT exam is to be conducted in descriptive mode? Ans No, this exam is to be conducted in MCQ pattern only. It is proposed to ensure avoiding any
arbitrariness or human bias, while evaluating the answer scripts,
7 Whether the CBT exam is to be conducted as Computer Based Test or can be conducted in manual
mode also? Ans Computer Based Test is preferred to ensure objectivity. However, if the number of candidates are
very less or other logistic reasons, the exam may be conducted in manual mode also.

Online regular and advance course registration
1 If a student is willing to complete the courses in advance, is the option available? Ans Yes. A student can select a maximum of two Courses along with the regular courses of current
semester with the condition that these courses must be professional elective courses of the
immediately following semester.
2 Is Advance Course Registration (ACR) is applicable only for the courses in IV-II semester? Ans No. Advance Course Registration is available for all semesters, only one semester advance, if the
course pre-requisites are fulfilled by the student. The faculty mentors shall decide if the
prerequisites are satisfied or not. For example, if the Professional Elective is offered in III-I
semester, students can register for this course in online mode in II-II semester.
3 Whether the advance course registration is applicable for Core courses and Open Elective courses
also? Ans No. Advance course registration is Applicable only for Professional electives.
It is not applicable for Core Subjects and open electives.

It is not applicable for Core Subjects and open electives.
4 If a student fails the online course opted under Advance Course Registration, will it be considered
as supply or regular? Ans If a student fails in Advance Course Registration, it will not be counted as supply. However, if a
student fails in online course belonging to the current semester, it will be treated as supplementary.
5 Suppose a student opted MOOCs course under Advance Course Registration and fails, what are the
alternates? Ans If a student Opted an online course under Advance Course Registration and fails, the student has
three options to choose from:
Option 1: Register for the same MOOCs course, if offered next time
Option 2: Register for another MOOCS course from the Board of Studies approved course under
the same Professional Elective basket.
Option 3: Register for the actual Professional Elective course offered at the department (Physical
mode).

6 A Student completed the course in advance, what about the printing of grade Memo? Ans Though the student completes a course in advance, the grade of this course will be printed only in
the grade memo of the semester in which this course is offered.
7 Under CBCS, one or two courses can be advanced or postponed. Is this rule still applicable?
Now the advancement is proposed for a max of two PEs.
Can the student avail both the provisions? Ans The student will be overloaded if he/she registers for two additional courses as per CBCS and
register for two PEs in online mode.
Hence it is proposed to keep a cap on two. Accordingly, the student can register for either two
additional regular courses as per CBCS norms or two additional online PEs or one regular course

8 Can the student register for a Professional Electives course which is having a labs? Ans If the online learning platform provides theory teaching and simulated lab environment, then we
will permit the students to register for both the theory and lab in the online mode. If such provision
is not there the student shall be advised to register for PE and the associated lab in the conventional
mode only.
It is not recommended to have online course for theory and the corresponding lab as physical lab.

1 Can a student discontinue the Minor or Honor degree program once opted? Ans Yes. In such case only B.Tech. degree will be issued.
2 If the student secured the required credits for the award of B.Tech. degree but having one or more
backlogs in Minor, when can the student get his B.Tech. degree. Ans If the student wants B.Tech. degree immediately, he/she has to submit a declaration to the Principal
stating that he/she will forego the credits earned for the Minor program and receive only B.Tech.
degree. In such cases only B.Tech. degree will be issued. Alternatively, if the student wants both
the B. Tech. and Minor degree, he/she can clear the backlog subjects in Minor program and get
both the B.Tech. degree and Minor deg.
3 Can the courses under Minor / Honor Degree can be opted through MOOCs/ Online learning

5 What is the Minimum number of students requirement to offer Minor and Honor Degree Program Ans The Principals of the colleges need to take the call.
